messages.author: 2daf77131be27db0
messages.subject: raster UD
parts:
I am interested in analyzing change in weekly habitat utilization of birds monitored using GSM-GPS transmitters. I have some questions on using ctmm.

1) shouldn’t the sum of UD produce by occurrence () add up to  1 ?  In addition why sometimes raster contains NA values?

GUESS <- ctmm.guess( ind.tele,interactive=F)

FIT <- ctmm.fit (ind.tele, GUESS)

ind.UD = occurrence (ind.tele, FIT)

UD.raster =  raster (ind.UD ,  DF = "PDF") or “PMF”

sum ( UD.raster@data@values [ !is.na(UD.raster@data@values)] )

[1] 1.621909

 

2) as I have many monitored individuals, using ctmm will probably result in movement modeled differently based on best model fit. Is it correct to compare UD produced by different models? Wouldn’t it be more consistent if one model is used for all weekly UD?

3) What will be a good representation of change in utilized area “area of weekly movement”  UD produced by occurrence () or AKDE () , as I am interested in weekly movements?

4) as I am interested to look at the characteristics of heavily used sites, is it yet supported to use unified grid for all individuals? what is the best alternative to look at that ?

5) Is it possible to produce raster layers with unified resolution for all individuals?
Thanks,
Joseph

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: raster UD
parts:
Hi Joseph,

1) The sum of the probability mass function, option "PMF" should add up to a number very close to 1, with some truncation error. In the akde() function, there is an error argument to bound this truncation error, but it looks like I didn't provide that argument in the occurrence() function, so its presently just using the default error. I will fix that in the next version.

The sum of the probability density function "PDF" should add up to 1/pixel_area, also with truncation error.

I have no idea why the raster would have NA values, but I am not terribly familiar with that format. If you have a minimal working example, then I can take a look and at least see if the problem is on my end.

Also, if you load the raster package, the sum() method should be defined for raster objects, or ,without raster loaded, raster::sum() should work.

2) Its fair to compare outputs based on different individual models that were selected from the same (good) set of candidate models.

3) The area of the occurrence distribution provided by occurrence(), while frequently misused in the literature, is sampling dependent and proportional to your ignorance of where the individual was during observation. Individuals with better data will have smaller occurrence areas that conform more tightly to the movement path. The area of the range distribution provided by akde() is a long range prediction of what area the animal will use if they continue that same (weekly) behavior in perpetuity. This might not exactly be what you have in mind to measure, but it is at least biologically meaningful and not explicitly sampling dependent.

As far as what area the individual used (past tense) just over the week, lots of people talk about this concept in the literature, but neither range nor occurrence targeted UDs actually estimate this quantity.

4-5) For akde() this is presently supported by feeding in lists of telemetry and model-fit objects. For occurrence() I have not yet implemented this, but I can move that up the TODO list if someone really needs it.

Best,
Chris
